message: THIS PERSON IS TRYING TO DESTROY ME!

replies.text: No, no I am not. I am here to help you.

message: You...you sound like the others did before they lied.

replies.text: I know about the talisman. The folded coin.

message: Then you know why I can't come down. If it's gone...it will come back.

replies.text: I found it. I have the folded coin.
But I already gave it to you, remember?
Actually, I know about it, but I don't have it yet. Sorry.

message: You have it? Then throw it to me. Please. Don't come closer.
HELP!
She fumbles, then grips it tightly. Her breathing slows.
Safe...I forgot what that feels like.
Safe...I forgot what that feels like. I cannot stay here anymore.
Back to them. The others who waited. Meet me there. I do not walk alone now.
My name is Syrra. Thank you for bringing it back.
It's unsafe to walk on top of these large rocks.
HELP! SOMEBODY HELP ME!
STAY AWAY FROM ME!
I know. It still follows me. Just not as closely.

replies.text: Fear does not decide where you stand.

message: No. But it remembers. I will too.
It is.
Yeah, sure, twenty-five thousand and I take a couple of your fingers too?

You want the house for yourself? Now that is interesting. Most people shy away from that cursed glow, but I can see ambition in your eyes. Hm. I could let it go for forty thousand gold...but gold alone won't earn my trust. If I sell it to you, I need proof you can be useful to me.
There's a small matter I want handled. Do this, and the price will stay at forty thousand. Refuse, and I'll reconsider whether you're worth the trouble.

replies.text: What do you want from me?

message: If you want the house, I'll need proof that you can handle business my way. There's a card dealer who runs games in the back of the tavern here in Brimhaven. He operates because I allow it. That means he owes me a regular fee, call it an 'operation tax' if you will.

He's late. Bring me what he owes, and don't let him wiggle out of it. I want every bit of the five thousand gold. When you return with the gold, I'll know you're serious, and the deed will be yours for forty thousand more.

replies.text: I'll be right back. Keep that deed handy.

message: Sure thing! As soon as I see forty-five thousand gold, you will see the deed to the house. Remember, you have my 'operation tax' gold too.

replies.text: Forty-five thousand?! I don't have that kind of gold.
Here, take the fourty-five thousand and give me the deed and the key.

message: Ah...so this is for Nocmar? The man who couldn't pay his debt and lost everything. And now you want me to just hand it back? Hah! If he wants redemption, let him pay double what he owed. Fifty thousand gold, no less. You bring me that much, and I'll give you the deed and the key.

replies.text: Fifty thousand gold?! Are you nuts? How about twenty-five housand?
Fifty thousand gold? I don't have it.
Here, take the fifty thousand and give me the deed and the key.

message: A pleasure doing business with you.
Well, then you better go find it.
Do you hear it now? The world hums with the memory of its first breath. Silence was never the absence of sound...it was waiting.

Kazaul'te varmun iktel urul.
Klatam ur turum Anavrin.
Kazaul'thra mor'gul ven'taar.
Uruk tharum vel Kazaul'ten mor.
Kazaul hamat urul.
Kazaul'the vurmor Anavrin urthaal!

The acolyte exhales, its voice fading to a whisper. The silence...broken...Its body turns to dust, carried away by unseen breath as the air shudders with awakening power.

So...the Fifth Master breathes once more.
You have undone silence itself, mortal. The rift shall open again, and through it we will see our dominion restored.
The Kazaul acolyte stands before Anavrin's shrine, its hands trembling as it unrolls the aged parchment. The air grows colder, shadows stretching across the floor.
The acolyte begins to read from the pages, the syllables harsh and alien.
Kulauil hamar urum Kazaul'te...Kazaul hamat urul...Klaatu ur turum Kazaul'te!
The parchment disintegrates in its grasp. The acolyte trembles violently, energy surging around the shrine.
You have done as we asked. The ritual of Five Aspects is complete...and with it, truth returns to the world.
The Shadow that your kind worship is not what you believe. It is no benevolent guardian, no path to balance. It is the echo of our masters...the Kazaul.

replies.text: That cannot be true. The Shadow guides and protects.

message: Believe what soothes you. Denial is the comfort of the living. But when you walk in its darkness again, listen...and you will hear our voices in its breath.

replies.text: You lie. The Shadow is not Kazaul.

message: Perhaps. Or perhaps you already know the truth, but your heart fears its shape. Leave now, child of dust. The Fifth is awake, and the world will not remain silent much longer.
Good work, my friend. You have saved Dhayavar.
You shall have your reward. But first you shall know my secret: I was the twelfth shade.

Worry not, fear not - I shall not harm you. When I said that in the confusion of the War, us shades hid, that's not strictly true. An Elytharan mage caught up with me, who was about to be the last to hide. She could have killed us, but I think her energy was nearly spent.

Instead she told me: "Until now, you have sustained fantasies in which you are the adventurers in magic, the pioneers in a new form of magic. Comforting daydreams in which you are always right. But no more. The fantasy is over. I have taken it away. For this is my judgement upon you: that you shall know, from this moment on, exactly how craven and selfish and monstrous you are."
Her spell stripped away my justifications. It made me realize what a monster I was.
Then she said - when your erstwhile colleagues, who hide now, are neutralized, you shall find peace. So $playername, thank you for liberating me.
Wear it if you want to overcome the resistance of the Kha'zaan shades. It should let you get past their safeguards.
So the Holy One gave you a ring.
I told you already, wear the ring that the Holy One give you if you want to overcome the resistance of the Kha'zaan shades.

replies.text: Oh, yeah. I will try that now.

message: You foolish child. Buried here are the shades of the Kha'zaan. You must destroy them.
Child...you cast aside the Holy One's blessing? Retrieve the ring from where you left it. Only then can I complete what must be done.
You're back so soon?

replies.text: I'm getting thrown out of Undertell.

message: Try again. Harder this time.
The Holy One gave you a relic did it not? Bring it to me.
You foolish child! Long were buried here the evil souls of the Kha'zaan. No one was to come here near these shades. Now your presence shall free them to wreak havoc on Dhayavar.
Wear the ring that the Holy One give you if you want to talk to me.

replies.text: Oh, you now too? Let me put it on now.

message: What have you done? Don't you realize the evil you have unleashed. Thanks to an Elytharan mage, my soul which was to be liberated, is now getting reinfected.
What you don't realize is that I was the twelfth shade.

When we were about to go into hiding, an Elytharan mage caught up with me. She stripped away my fantasies of being a pioneer in a new type of magic: Kazaul's magic, and laid bare what I had become - a monster.
Before I depart, child...the blessing must be passed on. Give me the ring granted by the Holy One.
As you have truly vanquished the Kha'zaan and resisted their whispers, Elythara grants her favor. Through this ring, her blessing now flows anew.
You're back again without the job being completed?

replies.text: No luck. I'm still getting thrown out of the caverns.

message: Try once more.
Now, no thanks to you, my soul has become reinfected, and we shall lay Dhayavar to waste, starting with you.

replies.text: I was hoping that it wouldn't come to this.

replies.text: I was hoping that it wouldn't come to this.

message: Child, if you knew the history of the world of Dhayavar, you would know how this place came to be. How the Lethgar were subjugated to Kazaul's will. How a few of the Lethgar became interested in the Dark Sorcery of Kazaul.
The past is never dead. It is not even past.

As you wish. So those Lethgar who were interested in the Dark Sorcery became none other than the Kha'zaan. Word spread that the Kha'zaan, through their devotion, were among the strongest followers of Kazaul.

replies.text: The Kha'zaan were defeated in the War of Dawn, weren't they?

message: Devotion. Remember that word. It holds more power than you think.
Through devotion, even if the Kha'zaan lost their corporeal forms, they became incorporeal shades. And survived.

During the confusion of the War, this section was overlooked. As the Elytharan mages cleansed Dhayavar, the war reached Undertell and was fought in these passages. Spells and counterspells everywhere. In this confusion, the shades hid here, weakened but alive. And here they remain.

replies.text: Let them be. I will just search for my brother Andor and get out. Tell me what to avoid.

message: If only it were that simple. These shades gain strength from the life force of the living. As no one has come here, and you are the first, they shall awaken. The longer you stay, the stronger they will grow. Soon enough they will escape these passages and haunt Dhayavar once more.

replies.text: What do I need to do?

message: You must destroy each shade you encounter in this cavern. There were twelve who hid here. You should find eleven of them still around.
There is not much time to tell you more. The shades grow stronger. Go hunt them! May Elythara bless you.
You are back once more!

replies.text: It is no use. They are just making me disoriented. Maybe I should give up?

message: Not if you want to save your brother, your family and Dhayavar.
Let me think...
In the town of Sullengard, there is a statue of Elythara. Pray to her for aid.

replies.text: That is the statue of Elythara? So close to Nor City?

message: Sullengard is a riddle bound in contradiction. Though it stands as the southernmost town sworn to the light of Elythara, it does not bend the knee to Feygard. Its people hold Feygard in quiet contempt, for its levies, its corruptions, its heavy rule, and the favoring of blood over merit. They veil these sentiments behind courteous silence, and so to outsiders they seem neutral. Even the statue bears no name. It is spoken of only as the Holy One.

replies.text: And me praying will not kick a hornet's nest?

message: No one will notice. Except maybe a few kids.
O Holy One, Preserve Us.
Why did you have to come here?

replies.text: I need clarity. What am I supposed to be doing?

message: Child, I will tell you later. Not enough time to tell you. Go hunt!
Now, no thanks to you, my soul has become reinfected, and we shall lay Dhayavar to waste, starting with you.

replies.text: Today, you will be removed from this world.

message: Memory of the self endures first. Pain follows identity. Systems are not remembered, they are endured. You must listen again.
Then you heard structure without belief. A system reveals itself through repetition. You must listen more.
Silence is not absence. It is what remains when speech was never permitted.

Then you have more than one account. That allows comparison, but only if you listen for what does not repeat. Systems reveal themselves at their edges. Return. Do not seek another voice. Seek the limit of speech itself
I asked you to listen, not for stories, but for failure. If Undertell erased the Elytharan deliberately, it would not do so in only one way. Return. Listen for difference.

Undertell!
That book was written carefully. Not to preserve truth, but to survive being questioned.
The Aewatha Kingdom was meticulous in year four hundred and thirty-two. Stone was counted. Labor was measured. Voices were not.

The Elytharan followers sent into those mines did not vanish. They were made unrecordable. If even one of them still remembers themselves, then this book is incomplete. You have already walked Undertell. Return and listen for what the pages avoid.

replies.text: I will return to Undertell and listen.

message: Of course they do. History records stone and steel, but memory lives in people even after death. You have given voice to what was buried. That is worth more than any written account.
Definitely. Count on me. Glad you could help him, the poor sod.
What is more important than a kidnapping?

replies.text: Please keep these 4850 gold coins for safekeeping. Rain has asked for you until he gets over his hangover, he'll come collect them when he is ready.

message: W-w-w-well?
W-w-whatever y-y-you say.

replies.text: You need to pay Shannal's descendant.

message: I have to pay this person? How can you be serious? Look at me, I just recently got of that Feygard prison. I don't have any gold.
All I have is fifty gold, I swear of it.

replies.text: Are you kidding me? Let me call the ghost - she must be nearby...

message: N-n-no, I found some more in my other pocket. I have 500 gold.
H-h-how about a 1000?

replies.text: Old sins cast long shadows. Try harder.

message: You'll bankrupt me! Well, here's 5000. It's all my savings I secreted away before I was arrested and put in a Feygard prison.

replies.text: That should be enough. Stay out of trouble. You're safe for now.

message: What do you want?

replies.text: To show you this traders' coin.

message: W-w-w-where did you get t-t-t-that?

replies.text: A ghost near Galmore Mountain asked me to show it to you.

message: G-g-g-g-almore! I am dead.
Oh well, we're not proud of it. My ancestor was one of those who would force or capture people to work in the mines of Undertell. He would be paid in these coins to get these people.

replies.text: What is that coin? What does it mean?

message: Can't really say. We're not happy about it. He was the black sheep of the family.

replies.text: Like you're any better. The apple doesn't fall far from the tree.

message: A ghost asked you to show m-m-me? I'm dead. Since the ghost is here after all these years, it could be looking for revenge. My life for her suffering.

replies.text: Old sins cast long shadows. However, perhaps I could talk to her, ask her to spare you?

message: W-w-will you? T-t-t-thank you! P-p-p-please help me.
Have you t-t-talked to the ghost y-y-yet? P-p-please hurry.
...Unless you're not here to play. Don't tell me Alkapoan sent you for his damned tax again?

replies.text: Yes. He sent me to collect the operation tax.
You owe Alkapoan. I'm here to take what's his.

message: [Grumbles] Always the same story. Alkapoan's cut, never mine. Fine, here. Take your five thousand gold and tell him I'm clear...until next month.
Take what's his? Ha! He already bleeds me dry every month. How much is it this time?
Slams the table, six?! That greedy vulture...fine, here. Just get out before I change my mind.
Speak the names of the lost when you can. We were men once, not shadows in stone. That is all a slave could hope for.

replies.text: I will honor your memory by continuing my search.

message: That weapon...must you hold it where I can see it? Even in death I know its glow.
Wrong? To you it is a finely forged weapon. To us...it was an executioner's tool.
When the Shadow rose, many who came for the Elytharans carried heartsteel. It cut through armor with frightening ease, but that was never what we feared most.
Those struck down by heartsteel often found no peace. Too many never reached Elythara's embrace. Instead, they lingered...as you see us now.

replies.text: So these weapons created the ghosts?

message: No. The weapon was only a tool. It was those who wielded it, and the darkness they served, that filled our halls with restless souls.

replies.text: I never knew any of this.

message: I believe you. Had I thought otherwise, I would not have spoken with you. Keep your weapon if you must, but remember what it once meant to my people.
If you want to talk about something else, then please, get it out of my sight.
The pick is light in my hand and heavy in my memory. We were driven into the deep seams with only a lamp and a promise. Many never climbed back.

replies.text: What was it like down there?

message: Hardship was the only thing we owned. The mountain took the rest. But remembering us is enough. Few living souls do.

replies.text: I will remember that, but I must continue my search.

message: I will not speak while that glowing stone is in your pack. It stirs old pain. Set it down and return if you want my words.

replies.text: All right. I will set it down.

message: Sure, you do that.

Dark, cold, and full of smoke. The tunnels shook when the rock groaned. We dug at glowing seams until our hands bled. The overseers said the ore was precious to Nor City, though none of us were told why. We were tools, nothing more.

replies.text: Is there anything I can do to honor you?

message: My name was Brenor. I came from the lands ruled by Feygard, back when its people still followed Elythara. I was taken during the rise of Garthan I, when those who held to the Light were chained and sent below the mountain. I swung this pick as a slave until the stone claimed my breath.
Oh, sorry. Please don't tell Alkapoan that I hassled you.

replies.text: Now that's the attitude I like to see.

message: You look down again. The ghost stands where she was before: still, watching.
You say nothing.
You look down below to the first floor and you spot a ghost.
[Talking to yourself...]

replies.text: She ran away? Was it something I said?

message: The silence is so rewarding.
Then we can speak briefly.

replies.text: May I look at what's here?

message: You don't shout.
These were stored. Not claimed.
With Anoa fallen and the last of the Kha'zaan shades dissolved into silence, the cavern finally grows still.
The darkness born in the War of Dawn loosens its grip at last, leaving only the echo of what devotion once twisted.
Words trace in my mind like smoke. You carry the scent of heartstone. You did not ask the smith to shape a weapon from it. Why?

replies.text: I chose not to have a weapon forged.
That is none of your concern.

message: The air trembles as Falkour lowers his gaze to the box. For a long moment he says nothing, then exhales a slow breath that stirs the dust at your feet.

This scent...old fire and fear. I remember this relic. It passed through the hands of a mortal named Varnel, long before you walked this world. He fled these caverns clutching it as though it would save him.

replies.text: Varnel? Then this box is truly ancient. Can you open it?
You knew Varnel? How old are you, Falkour?

message: I will not open it myself. Some seals are meant to remain unbroken by my kind. But you...perhaps it is your fate to see it undone.

I lend you this fragment of me, not for greed but for truth. Take this claw. Its edge remembers the heat of the first forge. Use it to break the seal, and only the seal. Whatever sleeps inside will not thank you for waking it.

replies.text: Thank you, Falkour. I will be careful and find a safe place in this basement to open the box.

message: My child, I long ago gave up on counting the days. Hidden away from the sun, I have lost track of the passing years. The world above has changed many times while I slept.

replies.text: Then you must have known much of what came before?

message: The dragon lowers his head once more, eyes half-closed. A single claw, blackened and gleaming, lies on the stone between you. Its warmth seeps into your hand as you pick it up.
Disturbance wakes very old hunger. I rest because it is less costly to dream than to remember. If I rise, the world will remember dragons. That is not a kindness for either party.

replies.text: I understand. I will not wake you.
I must know more. Wake yourself.

message: Something vast lies curled against the far wall, scales dark as coal and steam rising from its nostrils. A thought touches your mind like a hand on a bell.
The dragon lowers a claw and nudges a small trinket toward you. It gleams faintly, warm but not burning. Take it, and keep your hands gentle with fire.

replies.text: I will wear it with care.

message: When the Rift opened, heat buried itself in rock and memory. I came seeking shelter from the hunger of its fires. I slumbered, and the humans rose above me, shaping houses and laws in ignorance. My breath found cracks and fed a small forge. I remain because the place holds what I once escaped. I do not leave what keeps me whole.

replies.text: I will go upstairs and leave you to sleep.

message: The dragon settles, and the warm hush returns. Its breath is a slow tide through the stone vents. The glow above you hums like a distant hearth. You climb the steps back to the house and the smith who waits there.
Counsel is costly, yet you have already shaped your path in flame. You carry a weapon forged from my breath; what more could I give? Go now, and do not let that gift burn the world anew.
You show restraint where many would choose blade. For that, I offer a token. Take it and wear it as a reminder: heat can be a cure or a curse.
Mortal flame...yet not born of greed. Why do you disturb my rest?
Thought is older than voice. I do not rise for passing curiosity. Speak plainly, child of ash and stone.

replies.text: Nocmar said you heat the forge above. Why do you live here?
I found this ancient box sealed tight. They say only a dragon's claw can open it.
I will not wake you. I only wanted to see.

message: To wake is to remember. If you insist, I will stir. But remember, not all that sleeps should be coaxed to waking.

replies.text: No. I will leave you be.

message: You press your palm to the warm scale and whisper whatever small plea your heart can shape. The great form shifts. Steam rolls across the chamber. A low hum grows into a thought that blooms in your mind.
You woke me. You risked the old truth. Why did you do it?

replies.text: To know why you live here.

message: Your answer tastes of sharp iron. I ask only to mark the heart of your choice. Walk in peace if you can. I will sleep on.
The bell has not rung.
When the bell rings, the bowls are filled.
The fire must be watched. The pots must not boil dry. When the bell rings, the bowls are filled.
Those who work, eat. Those who eat return to work. The bell decides.
When the bell rings, the bowls are filled.
Tell those ingrates over in the other room that their dinner is almost ready!

replies.text: [Lie] Sure, I'll do that right now.
What still needs to be done?

message: There is another. A girl. She never came back here when the shades fell. Instead, she hides east of here. Probably in a corner somewhere.
Fear does not listen to truth. She made something to keep it away.
A folded coin. Copper. She believed evil could be trapped if it could not breathe.
Lost. Taken. We do not know which. Only that it never came back.
You have not forgotten her, have you?

replies.text: I am still trying to understand what happened to the talisman.

message: They used to gather our things. Count them. Decide what mattered.
Those above us. Those who studied fear instead of ending it.
If the talisman still exists, it will not be with the dead.
With those who believed fear could be shaped. Go to the Masters.

replies.text: Don't worry, I will take care of this for you guys.

message: What are you doing here? Go find that talisman and bring it to her.
She came back. We did not think she would.

replies.text: I want to speak to her.

message: She is here because she chose to be. Not because fear left her.

replies.text: Then let me hear it from her.

message: Do not mistake silence for weakness.

replies.text: You do not have to hide anymore.

message: It is so wonderful to finally be free of the evil that surrounded those shades...thank you Elythara!

replies.text: What?! It was thanks to me. You guys are hopeless.

message: Yes! Freed from the rule of those Kha'zaan shades.

replies.text: But that was not Elythara. That was me.

message: Listen you, we've been hiding for Elythara knows how long, and the first thing you say to us is a lie?

replies.text: But it was me, I swear to Elythara it was me.

message: If that is true, then maybe you could help us help someone else?
Oh thank you Elythara! We are freed at last.
Is it that mead I ordered from the tavern?

replies.text: No, it's not mead. That's the last thing that you need.

message: Well, then I don't want it. Go get me some more mead from the lovely barkeeper, Bela.

replies.text: No. I have a potion that will make you recover. Shannal's ghost has asked that you drink it. Now drink it. [here, take it]

message: Shannal? That name sounds familiar to me, yet distant to me.
While leaning his head back, he downs the potion in one gulp...amazing.
Now I remember; it was horrible. [weeping]

replies.text: There...there...Shannal's ghost told me to tell you she's at peace.

message: Thank you! To have passed her life at that place, kidnapped against her will, away from her husband and kids...
Well, let me get on with life...I seem to have made a mess of myself.

replies.text: Worry not, as restitution, Shannal made the kidnapper's descendant, Benbyr pay up. Here's 5000 gold. Keep it and yourself safe.

message: Thank you! Please ask Bela to keep them safe till Rain, oh by the way, that's my name, gets over this hangover. I need new clothes. So I will take 150 gold and visit the merchant. Please give Bela the remaining 4850 gold.
Let me meet the merchant and then return. Please go meet Bela.
Among the dust and bindings, something dull catches the light. It is copper. Folded. Out of place.
It rests untouched, as if waiting.
You grab the coin off the shelf.
You notice some fresh footprints in the dirt.

replies.text: They are of no interest to me. Time to go back to my plans.
I think I should follow them.

message: "The Ritual of Five Aspects"? No, I can't say that I have. The name sounds ominous though. You're welcome to look through the shelves if you wish. Just be careful with the older scrolls - they crumble if you breathe too hard on them.

replies.text: Thank you. I'll take a look around.

message: A locked box? No, I've never noticed one. I've been in charge of these archives for years, but I suppose some things manage to hide from even the most watchful eyes. I'm afraid I don't have a key for anything like that.

replies.text: Do you know who might have the key?
That's all right. I'll figure something out.

message: Hmm...the church keeps spare keys in the rectory upstairs, I think. You might ask Skylenar - he oversees most of what's stored down here. But please, don't break anything. Those boxes could be older than Remgard itself.

replies.text: I'll ask him. Thank you, Gwendolyn.

message: This heartstone radiates unbearable heat, glowing faintly with the breath of the Rift itself. The surface scorches at the slightest touch, making it impossible to lift or carry.

replies.text: [thinking aloud] Maybe Unnmir knows what I should do next?
OK, it's time to see if Unnmir is right! [place the block of Galmore ice on the stone]
I have a great idea! Maybe this block of ice that I found on Galmore Mountain can be used to cool the heartstone?

message: Before you rests a massive, glowing stone, pulsing faintly with an inner light. The shape and markings leave little doubt: this is the heartstone you've been seeking.

You set the block of Galmore ice onto the blazing heartstone. At once, a violent hiss erupts, filling the chamber with steam. The ice cracks and splinters, melting faster than your eyes can follow until nothing remains but a shallow puddle on the stone floor. replies.text: Do you remember who sent it there?
So it was once here in Sullengard?

message: It was before my time, but the records say it came from one of my predecessors, the first priest to serve under the banner of the Shadow here. He noted that it was delivered to him by travelers claiming to have found it among the ruins to the west.

replies.text: Ruins to the west, perhaps where Varnel perished.

message: So it seems. It rested in our archives for generations, though no one could read it. When the scholars from Remgard offered to take it, we gladly let them. It felt unsettling to keep something no one understood.

replies.text: Then Remgard is where I must go next.

message: If you seek that ritual, Remgard's church library is where your path leads.
You are reasonable?

replies.text: Oh, for the purposes of this conversation? Yeah, yeah I am. I want to talk to Alkapoan, not you!

message: What do you want, foolish child?

replies.text: I've collected your 'operation tax' from the dealer. Now let's finish our deal.
[lie] I want the glowing white house. I need a place to hide from my parents.
Nocmar has sent me to get back what was once his.

message: So...the circle is whole again. I warned the others that some truths should remain buried. But curiosity always feeds the dark.

replies.text: I am looking for a folded copper talisman.

message: Another seeker of knowledge? Few survive long enough to regret such curiosity.

replies.text: I only want to understand what happened here.

message: An ancient presence hums behind your eyes.
Leave now, before you can't
So, you have found it. The Ritual of Five Aspects...it returns to us at last.

replies.text: You said this would seal the rift forever.

message: Yes...or so it must be believed. The power it binds will quiet the rift if spoken by the faithful. Bring it to the shrine of Anavrin, the Silent One. One of our lesser kin will meet you there to perform the rite.

replies.text: Then I will take it to the shrine.

message: No. Give it to me and I will give it to the kin. You have done what none of the living could. Do not fail now, mortal. The silence of Anavrin waits to be broken.

[The air grows heavy as the master studies you.]
You are bold to walk here. Perhaps bold enough to be of use. One of our own is missing. The fifth master, Anavrin, lies silent. The Ritual of Five Aspects was taken from us long ago. Without it, Anavrin cannot rise, and we cannot restore balance.

replies.text: You want me to find this ritual?

message: Yes. The Ritual of Five Aspects lies lost among your kind. Long ago, a mortal scribe named Varnel served the Kazaul, writing our words into form. But when fear took him, he fled with the ritual and hid among your people. Bring it back to us, and the Rift will be sealed forever. Fail, and your world will wither like ours.

replies.text: I do not trust you, but I will look.

message:
[The master's eyes flare with dim light.]
Then go, mortal. Seek the lost ritual. In the ruins of your kind lies our key to completion. Return only when it is found.
You talk to me. She doesn't talk to mortals such as yourself.
"She" is a campanite, a pet if you will...yeah, my guard pet and not an "it".

replies.text: A pet? I want a pet. Where can I get a campanite for myself?

message: Kek-kek-kek-kek-KRAAAK!
The creature lunges forward...you pull back moments before it clamps onto your hand!
What is wrong with you?

replies.text: Nothing. I'm just happy to still have ten fingers!

message: Are you giving up? Is it time to leave?
Do you want to enter the Lake of Fire?
In front of you sits an ancient-looking crate filled to the brim with gold coins.
Do you want to risk your life by looting it?

replies.text: Risk my life, over some coins? No, I do not think so.
Of course I do. I'm poor and really need these coins.

message: Do you want to loot it and risk upsetting the masters?

replies.text: Of course I do. I'm poor and really need these coins.
I am $playername, I fear no master.
No, I do not. Those masters could end my life.

message: While stuffing the gold into your coin purse, you try counting the coins..twenty-one hundred coins!
The crate has been picked clean; only scuffed wood remains where the gold once lay.
Beneath your feet, you notice a pickaxe. Do you want to pick it up?
Kneeling down, you push aside loose dirt with your fingers, you pick up the pickaxe.
A wooden crate rests ahead, cracked along its sides. Coins are piled high inside, rising above the rim and catching the light.
Loot the crate?

replies.text: No way! Coins do not get left out in the open like this. They are almost always hidden.
You bet I do! I will take the risk and steal these babies.

message: The crate has been picked clean; only scuffed wood remains where the gold once lay.
You examine the coins more closely. Their surfaces show small imperfections.

replies.text: [talking to yourself] I think someone has used these. I can see the wear along their edges.

message: The markings are precise, but unfamiliar.

replies.text: [talking to yourself] They could pass as real...or they were made to. Are these fake? I don't really know either way, I will keep them.

message: You reach into the crate. The coins slide together with a familiar sound.

replies.text: That sounds right. They feel solid in my hand...which does not mean much.

message:
You step into a chamber where nothing is displayed for reverence. Every object is placed as if awaiting judgment. The air is still, yet your body refuses to fail.

You are not being protected. You are being allowed.
You can't proceed any further with these barricades in your way. Maybe there's a way to remove them?
While laughing uncontrollably...
You're going to need help getting past those barricades.
You shouldn't sleep here...not yet anyway.

A skeleton lies collapsed across the stone pavers beside the mining rails. The skull is turned toward the rock wall, as if the adventurer's final moments were spent facing stone rather than escape. A dark pool of dried blood has settled into the grooves between the stones and along the base of the rail.
The bones are spread unevenly, suggesting a fall followed by stillness. Scratches mark the stone near the wall - shallow, uncertain. Whatever happened here ended quickly, but not without awareness.
You carefully sift through the remains...

A book is lodged near the ribcage, its oilcloth wrapping stiff and darkened with blood. Despite the damage, the title remains readable: "Undertell: Its Ghosts and History".

But there's more...
Near the wall, half-hidden by bone and shadow, lies a necklace. Its chain is caught between two stones, the metal worn smooth by travel. You know this necklace! It's the "Jewel of Fallhaven."
You step back toward the table, aware now of how deliberately the crown was positioned and decide to return it.
You step back toward the table, aware now of how deliberately the crown was positioned and decide to return it.
You return the crown to its place at the center of the table. The room settles into its intended stillness.
There's nothing left to do here without the crown.
Resting alone upon a stone table, lies a crown. It is not shelved, nor sealed away, but left exposed, as if meant to be examined again and again.
As you lift the crown from the table, the space around it feels suddenly incomplete, as though the room was arranged with this absence in mind.
Much to your dismay, the chest  is empty.
A ghostly miner leans heavily on a spectral pickaxe, using it as a cane. His faded eyes glimmer faintly in the warm air of the tunnels.
Durnan...once of the Lethgar. This pick carried me through life, now it props up what's left of me.

replies.text: Do you remember anyone named Varnel?
I have to go now, but it was nice talking to you.

message: Varnel...the scribe. He was no miner, yet they made him dig beside us. Always scribbling between swings. Said he wrote words to keep them from the Masters.

replies.text: Do you know where he went?

message: East, through the lower caverns. He spoke of a town where the sun still touched the Sutdover River. Said he would hide among its people until the voices of the Masters faded from his dreams.
If you find what he carried...bury it deep, far from here. The chains broke too late for us. Now...let me rest.
A little dazed and a lot confused, you pick yourself up off of the ground only to find that you are no longer in Undertell.
The shade did not try to kill you. It simply removed you.

replies.text: [talking to yourself] I guess I should talk to Anoa?

message: A lot annoyed, you pick yourself and your stuff off of the ground and accept the trip to Undertell is needed once again.
The shades do not fight. They just keep sending you away.

replies.text: [talking to yourself] Anoa better know the answer!

message: A little annoyed, you pick yourself up off of the ground only to find that you are once again not in Undertell.
Once again, displacement occured.

replies.text: [talking to yourself] I guess I should talk to Anoa? Maybe he will be more helpful than before?

message: You've come back to visit me?

replies.text: Yes and I am really hoping that you can help me! I found the heartstone, but it burns to the touch. I cannot carry it.
I don't want to hold you from your busy day. I will leave now.

message: Too hot, you say? Hah, that makes sense. The heartstone has been sitting near that cursed rift for centuries, soaking up its heat. No man alive could carry it as it is. But there is a way. Back when I still walked the high trails of Galmore, I heard of a rare ice found only near the mountain's peak...

They called it "Galmore Ice". Unlike any common frost, it does not melt in your hand or in the lowlands. Only the hottest fire, or something born of the Rift itself, can turn it to water. If you can get your hands on a block of it, place it upon the heartstone. The ice will cool the stone, and in melting, make it safe enough to carry.
Climbing to that height is no small task, and the beasts there guard it jealously. But if you truly want to see heartsteel reforged, you'll need to brave the peak. No one else can do this but you.

replies.text: Great. Thanks. That helps a lot.

message: Unnmir leans back, shaking his head.
And?

replies.text: And he had this book. [show the Undertell history book] I was hoping for your insight.

message: If that book matters, someone in Fallhaven should know why.
Someone with a lot of books, I presume.

replies.text: OK, you don't know then. Thanks anyway.

message: A broad, luminous stone sits half-embedded in the cavern floor. Warm light swirls beneath its surface, shifting like embers stirred by an unseen breeze.
Its size and presence leave little doubt - this must be what you came for.
Before you lays a stone strikingly similiar to the one you already have, but this one is unrefined and can't be moved.
As you lean down to place the stone, a sharp crack echoes through the cavern behind you...
You flinch and the heartstone slips from your hands and shatters across the ground.
Where the luminous stone once laid, now lays only the stone's ground impression.
I felt the pulse the moment it stirred. Death is restless again. I welcome the silence no more.
Vaelzahr's voice is a rasping whisper.
Mortality remembers pain. Even now, your blood knows me.
The walls pulse faintly, as if the stone itself had veins. A deep, rasping voice speaks within your chest.
You arrive carrying an echo that is not yours.
Your kind drags history behind it, even when it thinks it walks alone.

replies.text: You are being vague on purpose

message: You carry what your kind calls an Oegyth crystal.

replies.text: So you know what it is?

message: This spot is just as good as any other to unlock this box.
After placing the claw in the keyhole, the box lights up red and crumbles in your hand. Revealing an ancient parcment in your hands.

The air thickens with heat as you descend the narrow stone steps. Each breath feels heavier than the last, carrying the faint taste of smoke and iron. At the bottom lies a vast, shadowed chamber, lit only by the dull orange pulse of fire leaking through cracks in the stone floor.
Something enormous stirs at the edge of sight - scales blackened by soot, breath slow and deep. The warmth here doesn't come from any forge...it comes from him.
A voice echoes inside your mind, as soft as the crackle of a distant flame.
Oh, a human child, here? How did that come about?

replies.text: Shannal let me through. Can I ask you, why do you look different than the others here?

message: Oh no. Just as I feared.
Like I feared. He was up to no good.
Saki seemed kind, even gentle. But there were inconsistencies in his stories. I assumed they came from the loss of memory that follows death. I was wrong.
Saki was no follower of Elythara. He sought to absorb the spirits of the Elytharan mages and draw power from them. I fear he serves the Kazaul, and he must be stopped.

replies.text: By we, do you mean me?

message: Unfortunately, yes.
Saki is trying to flee Undertell. Find him, defeat him, and recover the soul pearls and anything else he carries. Bring them back here.

replies.text: Looks like no one can be trusted.

message: In the end, trust is still required. Without it, we would already be lost.
It is not ordinary ore. Heartstone drinks the breath of the Rift and holds it. They wanted it.
Long ago, the first King of Nor City, Garthan of House Houdart, sent men into Galmore to pry at the mountain. They prized what they pulled from the mountain, though few ever speak plainly of why.

replies.text: What did they want it for?
Thank you. That is enough for now.

message: Power and profit are plain reasons. Old families in Nor City desired advantage. That is what men call progress and what others call cost. Remember this when you carry the stone.
This is what happened when he died [point to the man at the table]. That is what happened when they died [pointing east]. It's all very personal.
Oh, sorry, child. I am not knowledgeable about such things.
You carry questions like coins. Ask them, child.

replies.text: What is this heartstone everyone speaks of?
I found a book about Undertell. Do you know it?
I found these coins [showing Ysrine the rare coins] here in Undertell. Are you familiar with them?

message: Good - you're back...
but unfortunately you've come empty handed. How did you manage to drop them on the way back?

replies.text: Don't be so judgemental. They are really heavy, so I didn't want to carry them around with me.

message: and you have brought the Soul pearls.

replies.text: What do I do with the Soul pearls?

message: Go get them and bring them back here!

Besides keeping them away from those Kazaul Masters? I do not know yet. Powerful they are - they could perhaps bring Elythara back, help her re-establish her Dominion on Dhayavar.
Those Pearls might be the key to bring Elythara back, and balance out the power of the five Masters. Let the wisdom of your travels guide you.
This is no time to be fooling around. Please get those pearls back.
Thank you! It's because of you that we are rid of the remnants of the Kha'zaan. On that note, there's someone here to meet you.
Here, on my left.
Then you walk a quieter road than most.
Written histories come easily to stone and steel. They are less kind to breath, fear, and hunger.

replies.text: It feels like something is missing.
A book collector from Fallhaven asked me to listen to the ghosts of Undertell.

message: What is measured can be counted. What is endured must be remembered. Undertell has little love for the latter.

replies.text: You think the book leaves things out?

message: Those who suffered here were tools, not witnesses. Tools are used. Witnesses are avoided.

replies.text: I should keep that in mind.

message: The dead are accustomed to being spoken for. Few think to listen instead. Undertell remembers those who do.
You have spoken with one of them, haven't you? Their words cling to you. Be careful what promises you keep down here.

replies.text: They spoke of balance. I am not sure what they meant.
I did. Do you know what they want?
I wanted to talk about something else. The Kha'zaan to be specific.
I wanted to talk about something else. The Kha'zaan to be specific.
I found a book about Undertell. Do you know it?
Actually, I want to talk about Saki.

message: Balance can mean many things. For them, it once meant chains and silence. Listen closely, but never forget they speak for themselves, not for you.

replies.text: I will keep that in mind.

message: No one truly knows what the Masters want anymore. Even they may have forgotten. Just remember this: "truth and deceit sound much the same when spoken by the dead".

replies.text: You sound like you don't trust them.

message: Trust is for the living. Down here, it's better to doubt everything, even me.
Mortality's coil burns anew. The flame remembers what it once devoured.
The embers within Zaroth's hollow ribs flicker violently.
Flame does not merely destroy. It remembers what it consumes. Tell me, traveler, do you fear what endures through fire?

replies.text: I fear nothing born of heat or ash.

message: The chamber flickers with living fire, casting shadows that dance across Zaroth's scorched form. His eyes burn like twin embers as he studies you.
Yes, yes you are and a foolhardy one at that.
Carrying the very same weapon Geomyr banned?
